property_summary: After any call to Put, the unlockTime for the caller's account must be greater than or equal to the block timestamp at the time of the call, but the buggy version leaves unlockTime at 0.

After a call to Put, the caller's Acc.unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the buggy version sets Acc.unlockTime to 0, so when block.timestamp > 0 the unlockTime is strictly less than the block.timestamp.
After Put, the caller's unlockTime must be >= block.timestamp at call time; the mutant leaves it at 0, violating this for any non-zero block.timestamp.

After any Put call when caller later Collect()-s with a non-zero amount that is <= balance, the Collect must not revert due to unlockTime constraint, but the mutant leaves unlockTime=0 so Collect reverts when block.timestamp > 0 and _am > 0.

After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance must decrease by the collected amount; the bug leaves unlockTime at 0, making Collect revert when block.timestamp > 0, so balance is never reduced.

After any Put call, acc.unlockTime must equal the maximum of the provided _unlockTime and block.timestamp (or at least be >= block.timestamp when _unlockTime > block.timestamp); the bug always assigns exactly block.timestamp, so when _unlockTime > block.timestamp the unlockTime is lower than specified.
For any Put call, if _unlockTime is strictly greater than block.timestamp, then acc.unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp; the bug sets it to block.timestamp, violating this.

After any Put call, the value of `Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime` must equal the value returned by the public getter `Acc(address)` when called with `msg.sender`, which for the reference will be `max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)` and for the mutant will be exactly `block.timestamp`; the mutant breaks this by making `Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime` unconditionally equal `block.timestamp`.

For any Put call, if _unlockTime is strictly greater than block.timestamp, then immediately after the call, acc.unlockTime must equal _unlockTime; the bug instead sets it to block.timestamp, making it strictly less than _unlockTime.

After any Put call, the value returned by the public getter Acc(actor) for unlockTime must be strictly greater than the block.timestamp at the time of the call when the provided _unlockTime is strictly greater than block.timestamp; the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, violating this.

For any deposit via Put, the stored balance must equal the correct uint256 sum of previous balance and msg.value (checked addition); the buggy version allows overflow to wrap, breaking this invariant.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the contract's total ether balance (address(c).balance) must equal the sum of all recorded holder balances from Acc (sumAccBalances); the buggy version allows overflow in a holder's balance, causing the sumAccBalances to differ from address(c).balance.

After a Put, the holder's balance must equal the correct sum of the previous balance and msg.value as computed by the internal add_uint256 safe addition; the bug uses plain addition which can overflow, causing the stored balance to be strictly less than this correct sum when overflow occurs.
After any Put call, the holder's Acc balance must be at least msg.value; the buggy plain addition can overflow, making the stored balance less than msg.value.

For any Put call, the updated balance must equal the correct sum of previous balance and msg.value as computed by a safe addition that reverts on overflow; the buggy plain addition can overflow without revert, making the balance strictly less than the correct sum, which can be observed by comparing the stored balance to the safe addition computed off-chain.

The reference contract prevents reentrancy during Put execution, so the balance recorded after any external call during Put must reflect the full msg.value; the buggy version allows reentrant calls that can collect funds before balance is updated, causing the final balance to be lower than the sent value.

For any account that calls Put with a non-zero value, after the Put call completes, the recorded balance for that account in Acc must equal the sum of the value sent in the current call; the buggy version violates this because a reentrant Collect can drain the balance before the Put call updates it, leaving the final balance lower than the sent value.

For any caller with a nonzero balance and an unlockTime in the past that calls Put with a nonzero value, the contract's Ether balance after the call must equal the sum of its previous balance plus the sent value; the buggy version allows a reentrant Collect to drain the sent Ether back to the caller during Put's external call, leaving the contract's balance lower than expected.

After any Put call, the accrued balance of msg.sender in Acc must be at least msg.value; the bug allows a reentrant Collect within Put to drain funds before balance update, so final balance can be less than msg.value.

After any external call that results from a Put (specifically, to the Log contract), the caller's Acc balance must never decrease below what it was just after the msg.value was added; the buggy version allows a reentrant Collect during this external call to drain the balance, violating this invariant.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the contract remains non-locked (locked_ == false) so that subsequent Put calls can succeed, but the mutant permanently locks after the first call making further Put calls revert.

After any successful call to Put, the contract's reentrancy lock (locked_) must be released (false), allowing a subsequent call to succeed; the mutant permanently locks, making the second call revert.

After a call to Put, a subsequent Collect call that would otherwise succeed is permanently blocked because the reentrancy lock is never released, so the invariant "if a Collect succeeds under some conditions, a later identical Collect must also succeed" is broken.

After any call to Put, the reentrancy lock must be released (locked_ == false), ensuring the fallback function (which calls Put(0)) can always be executed successfully, but the mutant permanently locks, making the fallback revert.

After any call to Put that succeeds, locked_ must be false (i.e. the nonReentrant modifier properly releases the lock); the buggy modifier leaves locked_ true when a reentrant call causes an inner Put to reset locked_ to false before the outer call sets it back to true.

For any call to Put that completes without reverting, the contract's nonReentrant lock must be released (locked_ == false); the buggy modifier can leave the lock true after a successful call if a reentrant call resets it prematurely.

After any successful call to Put, the caller's Acc[caller].balance must equal the previous balance plus msg.value; in the buggy version, a reentrant collect during Put can cause the same msg.value to be added twice, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any input, after a successful call to Put, the contract's balance equals the sum of all Acc balances; the bug allows a reentrant collect during Put to update Acc balance without transferring ETH, breaking the invariant.

For any caller that never calls back into C during Put, after a successful Put, the contract's ether balance equals the sum of all Acc balances; the bug allows a reentrant Collect during Put to drain eth without updating accounts, breaking the invariant.
Collect cannot cause a decrease in the contract's ETH balance greater than the paid amount when the condition holds

When Collect is called, if the sender's holding satisfies the min balance, request amount, and unlock time, either the call succeeds only once (nonreentrant) or it reverts after reentrant calls drain the balance.
A successful Collect call that satisfies the conditions does not reduce the contract balance by more than _am.
If Collect is called with all conditions satisfied and does not revert, the caller's balance cannot change after the call side of the same transaction.
